title: Original finite Hamiltonian source-point precision audit
question: When the original finite oscillator Hamiltonian, coordinate basis, Gibbs state and projected graph are recomputed at arbitrary mpmath precision for the fixed R-426 row, does the residual gap remain separated from the R-422 reuse value without relying on the double graph snapshot?

new_perspective.principle: Move the precision boundary upstream: recompute the 16-dimensional oscillator coordinate basis and 256-dimensional volume-two Hamiltonian Gibbs state with arbitrary mpmath precision before forming the conditional graph row and residual operator.
route: Use the original R-419/R-416/R-402 finite formulas with exact rational fixture parameters, mpmath eigensolvers and 50 decimal digits; retain V=2, d=16, beta=8, right orientation, row 7 and tail threshold 4.
Construct the coordinate-basis momentum matrix, log-sum-exp coordinate Gibbs masses, conditional row and projected conductance directly from the high-precision source calculation.
Compute the blockwise weighted-zero-mean residual compression with a high-precision orthonormal basis and compare its first eigenvalue with the fixed R-422 and R-426 references.

Treat the result as a point-precision source audit only. Without interval arithmetic or certified eigenvalue enclosures, leave the original-source verdict unresolved even if a numerical separation is observed.
new_perspective.qft_bridge: Upstream precision can test whether the rounded-input boundary survives source reconstruction, but a point calculation does not provide a common core, regulator limit, physical sector or Yang-Mills result.

precision_contract.input_mode: original finite oscillator/Hamiltonian formulas with rational fixture parameters

required_methods: high-precision projected conductance and residual eigensolve

assumptions: The original R-419/R-416/R-402 finite oscillator and Hamiltonian formulas are the declared source model.
Fifty-digit mpmath eigsy and log-sum-exp arithmetic provide a converged point estimate for the finite source calculation.
The fixed conditional-row orientation, index, tail threshold and comparison tolerance are unchanged.
The residual basis spans the blockwise weighted-zero-mean subspace for the computed positive row.
missing_assumptions: Interval or ball-arithmetic enclosures for the 256-dimensional Hamiltonian eigenvalues/eigenvectors and coordinate eigenbasis.
A propagated enclosure for the conditional row, conductance and residual eigenvalue.
A basis-independent exact residual-reuse comparison for the original unrounded source.
A common unbounded Q3 core, regulator/volume-uniform estimate and history/OS/KMS/GNS/physical-sector transfer.
stop_conditions: If the high-precision source calculation cannot complete or fails positivity/normalization, classify this audit as blocked and preserve R-429.
If the source point residual is separated from R-422, do not call the original mismatch certified without an interval enclosure.
Never change the R-426 comparison tolerance or promote a point calculation to a uniform or physical theorem.
evidence_level: T0 / EXECUTED 50-DIGIT MPATH SOURCE-POINT AUDIT IF AVAILABLE; NO INTERVAL CERTIFICATION
non_claims: No interval or exact certification of the original Hamiltonian source.
No repair or closure of R-426 residual reuse for the original model.
No cutoff-, volume-, phase- or exhaustion-uniform Schur/residual bound.
No common core, history transfer, OS/KMS/GNS reconstruction, sector gap or continuum limit.
No C6, Sector-A, Pre-A, Yang-Mills or mass-gap conclusion.
boundary: R-430 moves the precision test through the original finite source formulas but remains a point-precision audit. Only a propagated interval enclosure can decide whether the R-426 mismatch is certified for the unrounded model.
next_unlock: Replace the point mpmath source calculation with interval/ball arithmetic for the coordinate and Hamiltonian eigensystems and propagate those enclosures to the residual gap at the same fixed row.

lean_crosscheck.role: R430 Lean checks scalar separation and the explicit no-interval scope; mpmath source reconstruction remains executable Python.
